exercises.name: Make Dm

params.fingers: index(1) on G? correct: index(1) on high-e 1st, middle(2) on B 3rd, ring(3) on G 2nd

exercises.coaching: Dm: index on the high e first fret, middle on the B third, ring on the G second. Low E quiet. The saddest, most useful minor in pop.

exercises.name: Minor progressions

params.note: for Am-F-C-G, put capo 0 and substitute F with capo? NO — teach Am-F-C-G using capo on appropriate fret; here we use C-G-Am-Dm (all open) and mention F via capo

exercises.coaching: Loop C-G-Am-Dm — all open chords, pure minor emotion. For the famous Am-F-C-G, you would use a capo (Lesson 14) since F is a barre chord we have not covered; today we stay on open shapes.

avatar_coaching_copy.intro: Major chords are happy; minor chords are the feeling. Dm is the most-used minor in pop. Add it and songs get emotional.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex1_intro: Dm: index on high e first fret, middle on B third, ring on G second. Low E quiet. That small shape carries a lot of feeling.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex2_intro: Loop C-G-Am-Dm — all open, all minor-ish emotion. The famous Am-F-C-G uses F, which needs a barre; for now we capo (Lesson 14) or stay on open shapes. The feeling is the lesson.
avatar_coaching_copy.results: Minor progressions give you the bittersweet songs. Dm is a small shape with a big emotional job.
avatar_coaching_copy.wrap: Dm in. Minor color unlocked. Lesson 18 we add fingerpicking — a whole new texture.
